description: Core Fleet Manager and OTA Update System modules with comprehensive unit tests. Creates forge_core/fleet.py (device registry, groups/tags, status tracking, fleet queries) and forge_core/ota.py (update packages from Phase 9 deployment packages, semantic versioning, rollout strategies, rollback, compatibility checking, per-device history). Both follow the established Manager class + JSON persistence pattern from model_registry.py and experiment.py. This FEAT must be completed before FEAT-002 (CLI + docs) which depends on it.
steps: Step 1 — Create forge_core/fleet.py: Define VALID_STATUSES = ('online', 'offline', 'updating', 'error'). Create a @dataclass DeviceInfo with fields: device_id (str), name (str), device_type (str), capabilities (list[str]), status (str, default 'offline'), tags (list[str]), groups (list[str]), last_seen (str, ISO timestamp), registered_at (str, ISO timestamp), current_model (str|None), current_model_version (int|None), experiment_id (str|None), metadata (dict). Add to_dict() and from_dict() class methods. Create class FleetManager(__init__(fleet_dir: Path|None=None) defaulting to PROJECT_ROOT/'fleet') with JSON persistence in fleet_dir/devices.json (same _load_registry/_save_registry pattern as ModelRegistry). Public methods: register_device(device_id, name, device_type, capabilities=[], tags=[], groups=[], metadata={}) -> dict — creates a new device entry, raises ValueError if device_id already exists; deregister_device(device_id) -> None — removes device, raises ValueError if not found; get_device(device_id) -> dict|None; update_status(device_id, status) -> dict — validates status against VALID_STATUSES, updates last_seen timestamp; list_devices(status=None, group=None, tag=None) -> list[dict] — filter and return sorted by device_id; add_tag(device_id, tag) -> dict; remove_tag(device_id, tag) -> dict; add_to_group(device_id, group) -> dict; remove_from_group(device_id, group) -> dict; update_device_model(device_id, model_name, model_version, experiment_id=None) -> dict — sets current_model fields on the device; get_fleet_summary() -> dict — returns counts by status, total count, list of groups, list of tags.

Step 2 — Create forge_core/ota.py: Import FleetManager, DeploymentManifest from edge_deploy, and ModelRegistry. Define VALID_ROLLOUT_STATUSES = ('pending', 'in-progress', 'completed', 'failed', 'rolled-back'). Define VALID_STRATEGIES = ('immediate', 'canary', 'staged'). Create @dataclass UpdatePackage with fields: package_id (str, auto-generated like 'pkg_XXXXX'), version (str, semver like '1.0.0'), model_name (str), model_version (int), source_package (str, path), requirements (list[str], device capabilities needed), created_at (str), metadata (dict). Add to_dict()/from_dict(). Create @dataclass RolloutResult with fields: device_id (str), status (str: 'success'|'failed'|'skipped'), previous_version (str|None), new_version (str), message (str), timestamp (str). Create class OTAManager(__init__(ota_dir: Path|None=None, fleet_manager: FleetManager|None=None) defaulting to PROJECT_ROOT/'ota'). Persistence: ota_dir/packages.json for packages, ota_dir/rollouts.json for rollouts, ota_dir/history/ directory with per-device JSON files. Public methods: create_update_package(source_package_dir, version, model_name, model_version=None, requirements=[], metadata={}) -> dict — reads manifest.yaml from source_package_dir if it exists to auto-fill fields, generates sequential pkg_XXXXX ID, stores in packages.json; get_update_package(package_id) -> dict|None; list_update_packages() -> list[dict]; check_compatibility(package_id, device_id) -> dict with 'compatible' (bool) and 'missing_capabilities' (list); create_rollout(package_id, target_devices=None, target_group=None, target_tag=None, strategy='immediate', canary_percentage=10) -> dict — validates package exists, resolves target devices from fleet manager (by explicit list, group, or tag), validates strategy, creates rollout record with sequential rollout_XXXXX ID, status 'pending'; execute_rollout(rollout_id) -> dict — SIMULATES deployment: for each target device, checks compatibility, updates device status to 'updating', then marks 'completed' (or fails subset for canary), updates device model info via fleet_manager.update_device_model(), records per-device results, updates rollout status. For 'canary' strategy, only deploys to canary_percentage of devices. For 'staged' strategy, deploys to all but marks as requiring confirmation; get_rollout(rollout_id) -> dict|None; list_rollouts(status=None) -> list[dict]; rollback_rollout(rollout_id) -> dict — sets rollout status to 'rolled-back', for each device with successful update reverts to previous_version, updates fleet device model info; get_device_history(device_id) -> list[dict] — reads from ota_dir/history/{device_id}.json; _record_device_history(device_id, record) -> None — appends to per-device history file.

Step 3 — Add version comparison utility to ota.py: Add a parse_version(version_str) function that splits semver 'X.Y.Z' into tuple (int, int, int) for comparison. Add compare_versions(v1, v2) -> int (-1, 0, 1). Use parse_version in check_compatibility to verify the update version is newer than the device's current version when the device has a current deployment.

Step 4 — Create tests/unit/test_fleet.py: Follow the class-based test pattern from test_model_registry.py. Include sys.path hack at top. Test classes: TestDeviceRegistration (test_register_device, test_register_duplicate_raises, test_register_with_metadata, test_register_with_tags_and_groups, test_initial_status_is_offline — ~5 tests); TestDeviceRetrieval (test_get_device, test_get_nonexistent_returns_none, test_list_empty, test_list_all, test_list_filter_by_status, test_list_filter_by_group, test_list_filter_by_tag, test_list_sorted — ~8 tests); TestDeviceStatusUpdate (test_update_status_online, test_update_status_updating, test_invalid_status_raises, test_update_nonexistent_raises — ~4 tests); TestDeviceTagsAndGroups (test_add_tag, test_remove_tag, test_add_to_group, test_remove_from_group, test_add_duplicate_tag_is_noop — ~5 tests); TestDeviceModelTracking (test_update_device_model, test_update_model_with_experiment_id — ~2 tests); TestFleetSummary (test_summary_empty, test_summary_with_devices — ~2 tests); TestDeviceDeregistration (test_deregister_device, test_deregister_nonexistent_raises — ~2 tests). All tests use tmp_path for fleet_dir. Total: ~28 tests.

Step 5 — Create tests/unit/test_ota.py: Follow the same pattern. Test classes: TestUpdatePackageCreation (test_create_package, test_create_package_with_manifest, test_sequential_package_ids, test_list_packages — ~4 tests); TestCompatibilityChecking (test_compatible_device, test_incompatible_device_missing_capabilities, test_version_comparison — ~3 tests); TestRolloutCreation (test_create_rollout_immediate, test_create_rollout_by_group, test_create_rollout_by_tag, test_create_rollout_canary, test_create_rollout_invalid_package_raises — ~5 tests); TestRolloutExecution (test_execute_immediate_rollout, test_execute_canary_rollout_partial, test_execute_rollout_updates_device_model, test_execute_incompatible_device_skipped, test_execute_sets_device_status — ~5 tests); TestRolloutRollback (test_rollback_rollout, test_rollback_reverts_device_model, test_rollback_nonexistent_raises — ~3 tests); TestDeviceHistory (test_history_recorded_on_execute, test_history_recorded_on_rollback, test_get_empty_history — ~3 tests); TestVersionParsing (test_parse_version, test_compare_versions, test_invalid_version_raises — ~3 tests); TestRolloutListing (test_list_rollouts, test_list_rollouts_filter_by_status — ~2 tests). Total: ~28 tests.
acceptance_criteria: forge_core/fleet.py exists with FleetManager class, DeviceInfo dataclass, and all specified public methods
forge_core/ota.py exists with OTAManager class, UpdatePackage/RolloutResult dataclasses, version comparison, and all specified public methods
FleetManager persists device data as JSON in fleet/devices.json using PROJECT_ROOT-relative default path
OTAManager persists packages, rollouts, and per-device history as JSON in ota/ directory
OTAManager.create_update_package reads manifest.yaml from Phase 9 deployment packages when source_package_dir is provided
OTAManager.execute_rollout simulates deployment, updates device status and model info via FleetManager, and records per-device history
OTAManager supports immediate, canary (percentage-based), and staged rollout strategies
OTAManager.rollback_rollout reverts devices to their previous model version
Running 'python3 -m pytest tests/unit/test_fleet.py tests/unit/test_ota.py -v' passes all new tests (~56 tests)
Running 'python3 -m pytest tests/ -v' passes all tests (272 existing + ~56 new = ~328 total)
findings: 56 new tests (28 fleet + 28 OTA) all passing. FleetManager persists to fleet/devices.json, OTAManager persists to ota/packages.json + ota/rollouts.json + ota/history/{device_id}.json. OTA reads manifest.yaml from Phase 9 deployment packages. Rollback stores previous_version as string (from int model_version). FEAT-002 can import FleetManager from forge_core.fleet and OTAManager from forge_core.ota. Version utilities parse_version/compare_versions are module-level functions in ota.py.
